title: LED Spectral Composition and Daily Light Integral for Energy-Efficient Basil Production in Plant Factory Systems: A Systematic Review
content: The demand for year-round production of high-quality crops has increased interest in plant factories with artificial lighting (PFALs). However, artificial lighting is a major energy demand in indoor production. This systematic review synthesizes evidence on the effects of LED spectral composition, photosynthetic photon flux density (PPFD), photoperiod, and daily light integral (DLI) on basil (Ocimum basilicum L.). The review focused on growth, quality, and energy-use efficiency. The review followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Sixty peer-reviewed studies were included from Web of Science, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar. Red-blue and broadband spectra supported high biomass production. Blue, ultraviolet, and selected far-red treatments modified phytochemical, essential oil, morphological, and quality traits. These responses varied with cultivar and lighting conditions. DLI influenced biomass and light-use efficiency. However, similar DLI values produced different responses when PPFD and photoperiod differed. Higher light inputs also did not consistently produce proportional gains in biomass or energy-use efficiency. Overall, efficient basil production requires coordinated management of spectrum, PPFD, DLI, photoperiod, cultivar, and production stage. An integrated lighting optimization framework is proposed to balance crop productivity, quality, and energy-use efficiency in PFALs.
